newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: EBNER'S BZ STILL SEES CS/WINTERTHUR OFFER AS FAIR.
newsitem.headline: EBNER'S BZ STILL SEES CS/WINTERTHUR OFFER AS FAIR.

text.p: Swiss investor Martin Ebner's BZ Group has not changed its view that a takeover offer from bank Credit Suisse Group for insurer Winterthur, where BZ is the biggest shareholder, is fair if not exceptional.
BZ executive Kurt Schiltknecht said the group believed the proposed merger was a good idea.

But Schildknecht said a decision on whether to accept CS Group's offer of shares must still be made by the boards of directors of BZ investment funds BK Vision and Stillhalter Vision, which hold Winterthur shares.
CS Group and Winterthur on Monday jointly announced that CS would offer 7.3 of its shares for every one in Winterthur if shareholders agree to the deal and to a capital increase at Credit Suisse.
BZ Group says it has about 25 percent of Winterthur with about another five percent held by BZ customers.
"Our two statements are very clear, I think," Schiltknecht said about the group's response to the takeovber plan.
"We think the exchange offer is fair but not extremely good. And we think the creation of this kind of bancassurance group is a good industrial solution," he told Reuters.

Bancassurance refers to the increasingly common melding of banking and insurance businesses as traditional divisions break down in the face of globalisation and stiff competition in financial services.
Schiltknecht said the group's position had not changed since its initial reaction to the merger plan.
"If some journalists put more weight on certain words or if people make their own interpretations, that is the risk that is always there," he said.

Schiltknecht declined to say when the boards would make a decision. The deadline is September 5, when extraordinary shareholder meetings of CS Holding and Winterthur will be asked to approve the deal.
"We will thoroughly consider these matters because we are not an institution that shoots from the hip," Schiltknecht said.
Ebner, Switzerland's best-known shareholder activist, is chairman of the separate three-man boards of the two investment funds. Schiltknecht is also a member of both boards.

Schiltknecht said BZ group was not worried about the fall in CS Holding shares since the takeover was announced, including a drop of 6.5 percent at Wednesday's close to 190.25 Swiss francs, a total decline of 8.7 percent this week.
"We don't really interpret day-to-day price swings. What is decisive for us is the medium-term trend," he said.
